front.tagline: The sacred queen of herbs found in every Indian courtyard.
front.ideal_spot: North-East or East balcony / courtyard

story.name_origin: 'Tulsi' in Sanskrit translates to 'the incomparable one'. In Hindu tradition, it represents Goddess Vrinda / Lakshmi.
story.cultural_context: Revered as an avatar of purity, its leaves are used in daily puja and brewed in kadha for immunity and cough relief.
story.fun_fact: Tulsi emits oxygen for nearly 20 hours a day and produces natural eugenol that keeps mosquitoes away from balcony doors!
story.symbolism: Spiritual purity, good health, and family longevity.

care_guide.sunlight_detail: Loves sunny balconies. Provide afternoon shade in extreme peak Indian summers (May-June).
care_guide.watering_method: Water in the morning. Keep soil evenly moist, but reduce watering during monsoon season.
care_guide.pro_tip: Pinch off the flowering seed spikes (manjaris) at the top so the plant stays bushy and thick.
care_guide.common_mistake: Overwatering during winter or placing in dark indoor rooms without direct sun.

front.tagline: The evergreen Vastu vine thriving in water bottles & balcony pots.
front.ideal_spot: South-East corner of the living room (Lord Ganesha direction)

story.name_origin: In Vastu, its heart-shaped leaves that climb rapidly upward are believed to attract wealth and continuous financial flow.
story.cultural_context: Found in almost every Indian living room in recycled glass bottles filled with water or climbing moss sticks.
story.fun_fact: You can grow Money Plant entirely in plain tap water without soil for years by changing the water every 10–14 days!
story.symbolism: Wealth, abundance, and positive energy.

care_guide.sunlight_detail: Loves bright filtered balcony light. Harsh midday direct sun will scorch its golden variegated leaves.
care_guide.watering_method: In soil: water when the top 1 inch feels dry. In water bottles: replace water every 10 days.
care_guide.pro_tip: According to Vastu, never let Money Plant vines trail along the floor—train them upwards on a wall or pole.
care_guide.common_mistake: Using chlorinated tap water straight from the tap without letting it rest for a few hours.

front.tagline: The soul of the Indian tadka, fresh from balcony to kitchen.
front.ideal_spot: West or North-West side of the balcony

story.name_origin: Called 'Meetha Neem' because its leaves resemble bitter neem but yield rich citrus-nutty aromas when tempered in ghee.
story.cultural_context: An indispensable seasoning for dal, sambar, and rasam, praised in Ayurveda for hair growth and gut health.
story.fun_fact: Feeding your Curry Leaf plant diluted sour buttermilk (chaas) once a month provides nitrogen that doubles growth speed!
story.symbolism: Nourishment, protection, and home warmth.

care_guide.sunlight_detail: Loves warm Indian weather and maximum sunlight. Slows down growth during cold North Indian winters.
care_guide.watering_method: Water deeply until water drains freely from the pot base. Let soil surface dry slightly between waterings.
care_guide.pro_tip: Prune the main stem once a year during spring to force multiple bushy side branches.
care_guide.common_mistake: Overwatering in winter or using heavy non-draining clay soil without cocopeat/sand.

front.tagline: The home Ayurvedic doctor for instant skin and hair care.
front.ideal_spot: North or East balcony for positive energy

story.name_origin: In Sanskrit Ayurveda, it is called 'Ghritkumari' ('young girl') because it was believed to preserve youthful skin and vitality.
story.cultural_context: Found on nearly every Indian terrace. The raw soothing gel is applied to hair before washing or rubbed on sun-exposed skin.
story.fun_fact: A single mother Aloe Vera plant will produce dozens of miniature clone pups around its base every monsoon!
story.symbolism: Natural healing, protection, and calm resilience.

care_guide.sunlight: Bright Sun to Partial Direct Sunlight
care_guide.sunlight_detail: Loves bright sunny balconies. If leaves turn reddish-brown, it is getting too much extreme summer heat—move to slight shade.
care_guide.watering_method: Soak deeply, then let soil dry out completely before watering again. During monsoons, keep away from non-stop rain.
care_guide.pro_tip: Always plant in terracotta clay pots with a drainage hole—plastic pots trap moisture and rot roots.
care_guide.common_mistake: Watering every day like a regular plant, causing leaves to turn yellow and mushy.

front.tagline: The tropical feather-frond tree that purifies urban apartment air.
front.ideal_spot: North-East or East corner of the hall

story.name_origin: A cousin of the Betel Nut (Supari) palm. Named 'Golden Cane' because its mature stems turn a warm golden-yellow color.
story.cultural_context: The staple decorative plant for Indian apartment living rooms, hotels, and entrance lobbies.
story.fun_fact: Ranked by NASA as a top air purifier and natural humidifier, releasing up to 1 liter of moisture every 24 hours in dry AC rooms!
story.symbolism: Peace, hospitality, and luxurious greenery.

care_guide.sunlight_detail: Place near a large living room window. Direct harsh midday sunlight turns green fronds yellow and scorched.
care_guide.watering_method: Keep soil evenly moist during summers. Reduce watering in winter and during the rainy season.
care_guide.pro_tip: Mist the leaves with a spray bottle twice a week to maintain humidity in air-conditioned apartments.
care_guide.common_mistake: Allowing standing water to sit in the base collection plate, leading to stem rot.

front.tagline: The 24/7 oxygen machine that survives weeks with zero water.
front.ideal_spot: South or West direction in bedrooms/halls

story.name_origin: Nicknamed 'Snake Plant' for its sword-like leaves with yellow borders and green patterned bands resembling serpent skin.
story.cultural_context: Extremely popular in urban Indian cities (Bengaluru, Delhi, Mumbai) for combating indoor AQI and pollution spikes.
story.fun_fact: One of the rare plants that absorbs CO2 and pumps out pure oxygen throughout the night, making it ideal beside your bed!
story.symbolism: Endurance, steadfast energy, and cleansing toxicity.

care_guide.sunlight: Low Light to Bright Indirect Light
care_guide.sunlight_detail: Extremely adaptable. Lives happily in dark bedroom corners, AC offices, or sunny balconies.
care_guide.watering_method: Water only once every 2-3 weeks when soil is bone dry. In winter or monsoon, water once a month.
care_guide.pro_tip: Wipe the leaves with a dry cloth once a month to remove city dust so it purifies air efficiently.
care_guide.common_mistake: Watering into the center crown of the plant. Always pour water directly onto the soil.

front.tagline: Fleshy jade-green coin leaves that attract wealth and good luck.
front.ideal_spot: Right side of main entrance door or North-East

story.name_origin: Known in Vastu as 'Kuberakshi' (the eye of Lord Kubera, treasurer of the Gods) because its oval leaves resemble emerald gems and coins.
story.cultural_context: Considered an auspicious gift during Diwali, Griha Pravesh (housewarming), and new business openings.
story.fun_fact: A Jade Plant can develop thick wooden tree-like trunks and live for over 50 years, looking like a miniature bonsai with zero training!
story.symbolism: Wealth attraction, prosperity, and enduring friendship.

care_guide.sunlight: Direct Morning Sun (3-4 Hours) + Bright Light
care_guide.sunlight_detail: Needs adequate light to keep stems sturdy and compact. In low light, it stretches and becomes leggy.
care_guide.watering_method: Check if bottom leaves feel soft before watering. Never water when soil is already wet.
care_guide.pro_tip: Rotate the pot 90 degrees every week so all sides get equal sunlight and grow evenly.
care_guide.common_mistake: Using regular heavy garden mud without sand/perlite; root rot is the #1 killer of Jade in India.

front.tagline: Fountain-style striped leaves with baby shoots hanging in air.
front.ideal_spot: North or East window / balcony ceiling

story.name_origin: Named for miniature baby offshoots that dangle from long curving stems like baby spiders suspended on webs.
story.cultural_context: A beloved choice for hanging pots on balcony grills across Indian apartments to create green privacy curtains.
story.fun_fact: A single healthy mother Spider Plant will produce 10–15 baby plantlets every season that you can snip off and pot for free gifts!
story.symbolism: Harmony, lightness, and positive opportunities.

care_guide.sunlight_detail: Loves bright shaded balconies. Harsh direct midday sun turns white stripes dull and crispy.
care_guide.watering_method: Water when topsoil feels dry. Its fleshy tuber roots store water, so it tolerates missed waterings.
care_guide.pro_tip: If leaf tips turn brown, switch from hard tap water to RO / filtered water to avoid salt buildup.
care_guide.common_mistake: Placing in dark corners with no light, which stops baby shoots from forming.

front.tagline: Native Indian giant with thick, leather-sheened bronze leaves.
front.ideal_spot: South-East corner of the hall or balcony

story.name_origin: Native to Northeast India (Assam and Meghalaya). The milky white sap inside its stems was historically tapped for natural latex rubber.
story.cultural_context: In Meghalaya, the aerial living roots of the Indian Rubber Tree are guided across rivers to form the famous 'Living Root Bridges'!
story.fun_fact: Its massive glossy leaves act like a magnetic sponge for indoor dust and airborne toxins, making indoor air noticeably crisper.
story.symbolism: Wealth, abundance, steadfast balance, and strength.

care_guide.sunlight: Bright Indirect to Gentle Morning Sunlight
care_guide.sunlight_detail: Needs ample bright light to maintain its deep burgundy-bronze leaf color. Near a large window is ideal.
care_guide.watering_method: Water thoroughly until water drains from the bottom. Let top 2 inches dry out before the next round.
care_guide.pro_tip: Wipe the thick leaves once every two weeks with a soft damp cotton cloth to preserve its mirror-like natural shine.
care_guide.common_mistake: Moving it around frequently; Ficus plants dislike sudden changes in location or light levels.

front.tagline: The calming white flag of peace that tells you when it is thirsty.
front.ideal_spot: Bedroom or Living Room North/West window

story.name_origin: Its graceful white hood-shaped bloom looks like a white flag of truce and surrender, earning it the name 'Peace Lily'.
story.cultural_context: A favored indoor gift plant for modern Indian homes for bedroom side-tables and air-conditioned living rooms.
story.fun_fact: Peace Lilies are famous communicators—if you forget to water it, the entire plant will droop completely flat, then perk straight back up 2 hours after a drink!
story.symbolism: Peace, calm tranquility, and positive energy.

care_guide.sunlight_detail: Perfect for rooms with gentle light. Keep strictly away from harsh direct sun which burns the white flowers.
care_guide.watering_method: Keep soil lightly moist. Water as soon as the foliage starts showing the slightest droop.
care_guide.pro_tip: Snip faded brown blooms with a clean pair of shears right at the base stem to stimulate fresh white blooms.
care_guide.common_mistake: Using hard alkaline tap water. If leaf tips turn yellow, switch to RO or filtered water.

front.tagline: The ultimate Instagram aesthetic icon with natural leaf holes.
front.ideal_spot: Living room near a balcony glass sliding door

story.name_origin: 'Monstera' means 'monstrous' in Latin for its massive split leaves; 'Deliciosa' refers to the sweet edible fruit it bears in the jungle.
story.cultural_context: The #1 plant seen in modern Indian aesthetic WFH desk setups, cafe decor, and urban plant parent reels.
story.fun_fact: The natural holes in its leaves (called fenestrations) evolved to let high-speed jungle winds pass through without tearing the leaf!
story.symbolism: Embracing your individuality and reaching for growth.

care_guide.sunlight_detail: Needs plenty of bright light to produce large leaves with fenestrations. Direct sun scorches the foliage.
care_guide.watering_method: Water thoroughly until it drains out. Allow the top 2 inches of soil to dry out between waterings.
care_guide.pro_tip: Tuck the aerial roots back into the soil pot as they grow to help the plant absorb extra nutrients.
care_guide.common_mistake: Keeping in a dark room; without bright light, new leaves will emerge small with zero split holes.

front.tagline: Mirror-shine black-green leaves with underground water tanks.
front.ideal_spot: Computer desk, bedroom side table, or dim hallway

story.name_origin: Short for its botanical name 'Zamioculcas zamiifolia'. The viral 'Raven ZZ' variety turns jet-black as it matures!
story.cultural_context: The holy grail plant for busy Indian techies and students who travel frequently and need zero-maintenance plants.
story.fun_fact: Its glossy mirror finish is 100% natural plant wax. Underground, it has potato-like rhizomes that store water for 4+ weeks of neglect!
story.symbolism: Endurance, silent resilience, and prosperity.

care_guide.sunlight_detail: Thrives under LED room lights or dark rooms. Avoid direct sun which turns the leaves pale and crispy.
care_guide.watering_method: Water sparingly once every 2.5 to 3 weeks. Soil must be completely dry before watering.
care_guide.pro_tip: Do not spray commercial leaf shine chemicals—just dust the leaves with a dry cloth.
care_guide.common_mistake: Overwatering. Yellow mushy stems are a dead giveaway that it's getting too much love/water.

front.tagline: Cotton-candy pink arrow leaves that brighten up any study desk.
front.ideal_spot: Study table, work desk, or bookshelf next to a lamp

story.name_origin: Named for its distinctive arrow-shaped leaves. The 'Neon' cultivar was bred to produce blush-pink foliage with lime-green undersides.
story.cultural_context: Huge favorite among Gen Z Indian plant collectors looking for pastel colors without dealing with difficult flowers.
story.fun_fact: As the plant matures, its simple arrowhead leaves transform and split into 3-to-5 finger-like lobes!
story.symbolism: Positivity, creative inspiration, and joyful energy.

care_guide.sunlight_detail: Needs decent indirect light to maintain its vibrant pink color. In low light, the leaves turn plain green.
care_guide.watering_method: Keep soil slightly moist. Water when the top 1 inch feels dry.
care_guide.pro_tip: Propagate by snipping a stem with a node and placing it in a cute glass test-tube vase on your study desk!
care_guide.common_mistake: Direct scorching sun which bleaches the delicate pink pigmentation into dull grey.

front.tagline: The braided green stalks that bring good luck to your study desk.
front.ideal_spot: College hostel desk, office workstation, or dining center

story.name_origin: Not actually bamboo! It is a species of *Dracaena* trained into spiral and braided shapes. 3 stalks = Happiness, 5 = Wealth, 6 = Health.
story.cultural_context: The #1 starter plant given to Indian college students and young professionals moving into their first PG/apartment.
story.fun_fact: In Chinese and Indian Feng Shui, Lucky Bamboo represents the balance of all five elements (Earth, Water, Wood, Fire, Metal)!
story.symbolism: Good luck, academic success, and smooth career paths.

care_guide.sunlight_detail: Lives happily under indoor room lights. Never expose to direct sun.
care_guide.watering_method: If grown in water: keep roots fully submerged in clean RO/filtered water and change water weekly.
care_guide.pro_tip: If stalks turn yellow, it is usually due to chlorine in municipal tap water. Always use drinking RO water.
care_guide.common_mistake: Letting the water dry up completely or placing in front of a cold direct AC air blast.

front.tagline: Cascading strands of living green pea pearls for macrame hangings.
front.ideal_spot: Hanging macrame planter on an East-facing balcony

story.name_origin: Named for its spherical bead-like leaves that look like a beaded pearl necklace cascading over the pot edge.
story.cultural_context: A viral aesthetic plant across Indian Instagram reels and Pinterest boho room makeovers.
story.fun_fact: The round spherical shape reduces leaf surface area to minimize moisture loss in hot arid climates; each pearl has a translucent 'window' stripe to let sunlight inside!
story.symbolism: Grace, precious memories, and artistic flair.

care_guide.sunlight: Bright Morning Sun (2-3 Hours) + Bright Indirect Light
care_guide.sunlight_detail: Needs good light on the top of the pot. Direct gentle morning sun keeps the pearls plump and tight.
care_guide.watering_method: Water from the bottom (submerge pot in water tray for 10 mins) when pearls look slightly puckered.
care_guide.pro_tip: Do not water over the top of the pearls, as trapped moisture between the beads can cause stem rot.
care_guide.common_mistake: Overwatering or planting in non-draining plastic pots without gritty succulent soil.

front.tagline: Fiery crimson-pink spotted leaves that thrive in air-conditioned rooms.
front.ideal_spot: Coffee table, TV unit, or bedroom corner

story.name_origin: 'Aglaos' (bright/shining) and 'nema' (thread) in Greek. 'Red Valentine' refers to its passionate pink-red mottled foliage.
story.cultural_context: Extremely trendy in contemporary Indian apartment interiors where people want colorful foliage without flowering hassles.
story.fun_fact: Aglaonemas are certified NASA clean-air champions that filter out benzene and formaldehyde emitted by modern furniture and paints!
story.symbolism: Passion, long-lasting joy, and modern elegance.

care_guide.sunlight_detail: Needs moderate indirect light to keep the intense pink-red splashes bright. Can tolerate low light.
care_guide.watering_method: Allow the top 2 inches of soil to dry out between waterings. Does not like soggy feet.
care_guide.pro_tip: Tolerates dry air-conditioned room air better than almost any other tropical colorful plant.
care_guide.common_mistake: Placing in harsh direct sunlight which bleaches the bright crimson color to pale white.

front.tagline: The architectural giant with giant violin-shaped leather leaves.
front.ideal_spot: Living room corner within 3 feet of a large balcony door

story.name_origin: Named 'Lyrata' for its stiff, violin-shaped (lyre) leaves with prominent geometric veins.
story.cultural_context: The gold-standard statement plant for upscale Indian urban apartments and aesthetic lifestyle creators.
story.fun_fact: Fiddle Leaf Figs are famous creatures of habit—if you move them to a new room or rotate them abruptly, they drop leaves in protest!
story.symbolism: Sophistication, pride, and personal achievement.

care_guide.sunlight_detail: Needs generous light to support its massive foliage. Place right next to your brightest window.
care_guide.watering_method: Water thoroughly until it drains freely out the bottom. Let top 2 inches dry between waterings.
care_guide.pro_tip: Gently shake the main trunk for 30 seconds weekly to mimic outdoor wind—this triggers the trunk to grow thick and sturdy!
care_guide.common_mistake: Drafts from air conditioners and moving it around the house too often.

front.tagline: Feathery neon-green cascading fronds that love shower steam.
front.ideal_spot: Bathroom window sill, balcony ceiling hanger, or shower ledge

story.name_origin: Discovered in 1894 among a shipment of ferns sent to Boston, rapidly becoming the staple Victorian parlor plant.
story.cultural_context: Hugely popular among Indian Gen Z creating 'indoor jungle' bathroom setups and humid balcony greens.
story.fun_fact: Ferns are prehistoric living fossils that evolved over 360 million years ago—predating flowers and dinosaurs!
story.symbolism: New beginnings, sincerity, and pure dreams.

care_guide.sunlight_detail: Prefers gentle filtered light. Direct afternoon sun will instantly crisp up its delicate feather fronds.
care_guide.watering_method: Keep soil consistently lightly damp like a wrung-out sponge. Never let it dry out completely.
care_guide.pro_tip: Hang it inside your bathroom near a window—it drinks the natural steam from your hot showers!
care_guide.common_mistake: Dry indoor AC air; if fronds shed and turn crispy brown, increase misting immediately.

front.tagline: Reptile-spotted leaves that fold up to pray every single night.
front.ideal_spot: Bedside table or study desk with gentle indirect light

story.name_origin: Named for its wavy, brushstroke-spotted leaves resembling a rattlesnake pattern, with deep royal purple velvet undersides.
story.cultural_context: The favorite subject for Indian plant timelapses on social media due to its dramatic day-to-night leaf movements.
story.fun_fact: Through a process called *nyctinasty*, its leaves spread flat during the day to catch light, then fold vertically straight up at twilight like hands in prayer!
story.symbolism: Gratitude, daily reflection, and mindfulness.

care_guide.sunlight_detail: Sensitive to direct sun, which curls the leaf edges and fades the striking purple underside.
care_guide.watering_method: Keep soil evenly moist. Sensitive to hard tap water salts—always use drinking RO water.
care_guide.pro_tip: Group it close together with other plants to create a natural high-humidity microclimate.
care_guide.common_mistake: Using cold tap water. Use room-temperature RO water to prevent leaf tip browning.

front.tagline: Sculptural exposed roots with a mini canopy for mindful focus.
front.ideal_spot: Center of your WFH desk or study table

story.name_origin: 'Ginseng' refers to the thick, pot-bellied aerial root trunk that resembles the Korean ginseng root.
story.cultural_context: The favorite starter bonsai for young Indian professionals to bring calm, zen vibes and stress relief to desk setups.
story.fun_fact: A cousin of the sacred Indian Banyan tree (*Ficus benghalensis*), it naturally develops miniature aerial roots that drape over its trunk!
story.symbolism: Wisdom, patience, grounding energy, and mental clarity.

care_guide.sunlight: Bright Indirect to Gentle Morning Sunlight (2-3 Hours)
care_guide.sunlight_detail: Loves plenty of bright light to keep its mini leaf canopy dense and compact.
care_guide.watering_method: Water thoroughly only when the top layer of bonsai soil feels dry. Never let it sit in standing water.
care_guide.pro_tip: Prune back shoots that grow beyond 4-6 leaves down to 2 leaves to maintain its picturesque miniature tree shape.
care_guide.common_mistake: Low light causing sudden leaf drop, or allowing roots to sit in stagnant saucer water.

front.tagline: The timeless queen of Indian gardens, from temple offerings to gulkand jars.
front.ideal_spot: Sunny balcony or terrace with 5-6 hours of direct sun

story.name_origin: 'Gulab' derives from the Persian 'gul' (flower) and 'aab' (water), literally meaning 'flower water'—a nod to the iconic rose water (gulab jal) distilled from its petals.
story.cultural_context: Integral to Indian culture—petals are scattered in puja thalis, strung into garlands for weddings, and used to make gulkand, rose sharbat, and ittar perfume.
story.fun_fact: Kannauj in Uttar Pradesh has been distilling rose perfume (ittar) for over 500 years using the same ancient 'deg-bhapka' copper-pot method!
story.symbolism: Love, devotion, beauty, and divine offering.

care_guide.sunlight_detail: Roses are sun-hungry plants. They need at least 5 hours of direct morning sunlight for prolific blooming. Afternoon shade helps in peak Indian summers.
care_guide.watering_method: Water deeply at the base in the early morning. Avoid wetting the leaves to prevent fungal diseases like black spot and powdery mildew.
care_guide.pro_tip: After each bloom cycle, prune spent flowers just above a 5-leaflet set at a 45-degree angle to encourage rapid re-blooming.
care_guide.common_mistake: Overhead watering that soaks leaves, leading to fungal black spots and powdery mildew in humid Indian weather.

front.tagline: The intoxicating midnight bloomer that perfumes entire Indian neighborhoods.
front.ideal_spot: East or South-facing balcony or terrace with morning sun

story.name_origin: 'Mogra' comes from the Marathi/Hindi word for its tight, layered bud form. In South India, it is 'Mallige' (Kannada) or 'Malli' (Tamil), woven into women's hair gajras every morning.
story.cultural_context: The soul of Indian evenings—mogra garlands are offered to deities, woven into bridal hair, sold by street vendors at traffic signals, and used to make jasmine attar and gajra strings.
story.fun_fact: Mogra flowers open only at night and release their strongest fragrance between 8 PM and 2 AM, attracting moths for pollination under moonlight!
story.symbolism: Purity, sensuality, divine grace, and marital bliss.

care_guide.sunlight_detail: Needs abundant direct morning sun to produce heavy blooms. In peak summer, provide light afternoon shade to prevent flower bud drop.
care_guide.watering_method: Water deeply in the morning until it drains from the pot base. Keep soil consistently moist during the flowering season (April-October).
care_guide.pro_tip: Feed with a handful of mustard cake (sarson ki khali) dissolved in water every 15 days during the blooming season for explosive flower production.
care_guide.common_mistake: Keeping indoors in low light—mogra will survive but refuse to flower without adequate direct sunlight.
